input.summary: The toolbox's `emphasis.iconStyle.borderColor` default is set to the exact same token as the normal `iconStyle.borderColor` (`tokens.color.accent50`), so hovering/focusing a toolbox icon produces no visible change. The fix is to give the emphasis state a distinctly darker/stronger accent token (`tokens.color.accent70`), matching the normal-vs-emphasis token pairing already used by the timeline component. No new public option is introduced — only a default value changes.
steps: NO TYPE/OPTION CHANGES NEEDED — verify only. `ToolboxOption.emphasis?: { iconStyle?: ItemStyleOption }` already exists at /workspace/src/component/toolbox/ToolboxModel.ts:66-68, and the per-feature mirror `ToolboxFeatureOption.emphasis?: { iconStyle?: IconStyle }` already exists at /workspace/src/component/toolbox/featureManager.ts:50-52. Do not add a new option name; this requirement is purely a default-value fix. /workspace/index.d.ts contains no toolbox/accent references, so it needs no update.

VERIFY THE TOKEN VALUES ARE ACTUALLY DISTINCT — /workspace/src/visual/tokens.ts:155 `accent50: '#6578ba'` and line 159 `accent70: '#404c76'`. These are two steps apart on the accent ramp, so the hover state renders a visibly darker stroke on the icon outline. `tokens.color.accent70` is a declared key on the `ColorToken` interface (tokens.ts:59), so TypeScript compiles without change.

CONSISTENCY CHECK (read-only, confirms the chosen token) — /workspace/src/component/timeline/SliderTimelineModel.ts already uses exactly this pairing: normal `controlStyle`/`itemStyle` at lines 79-80 and 113-114 use `tokens.color.accent50`, while `emphasis` at lines 130-131 uses `tokens.color.accent70`. Using accent70 for the toolbox emphasis makes the toolbox match the established normal→emphasis convention rather than inventing a new one.

CONFIRM THE VALUE ACTUALLY REACHES THE RENDERED ICON (no code change) — /workspace/src/component/toolbox/ToolboxView.ts:133 builds each feature model with `new Model(featureOpt, toolboxModel, toolboxModel.ecModel)`, so feature options inherit from the toolbox model. Line 173 reads `featureModel.getModel(['emphasis', 'iconStyle'])` and line 220 applies it via `pathEmphasisState.style = iconStyleEmphasisModel.getItemStyle();` on the `'emphasis'` state ensured at line 219. `getItemStyle()` maps the option `borderColor` onto the path's `stroke`, and `api.enterEmphasis(this)` on `mouseover` (line 275) activates that state. Nothing here needs editing — this only confirms the single default change is sufficient for the acceptance signal.

TESTS — there is no existing unit test covering toolbox icon styling. `grep -ril toolbox /workspace/test/ut/spec` returns only /workspace/test/ut/spec/model/Global.test.ts, and its single toolbox usage (line 818, the `innerId` test) only exercises the `dataZoom` feature's implicit dataZoom model creation and asserts nothing about colors. No test file needs updating. If you want coverage, add a case that instantiates a chart with a `toolbox.feature` and asserts `chart.getModel().getComponent('toolbox').getModel(['emphasis','iconStyle']).get('borderColor')` differs from `...getModel('iconStyle').get('borderColor')` — an invariant assertion is preferable to hardcoding '#404c76', since token hex values change across releases.

MANUAL VERIFICATION — open /workspace/test/toolbox-custom.html (or toolbox-title.html / toolbox-stack.html) in the dev server and hover a toolbox icon; the icon outline stroke must visibly darken from #6578ba to #404c76. Screenshot-based visual regression baselines under test/runTest may need re-baselining for any page rendering a hovered toolbox icon.
input.risks: Line numbers assume the pre-change tree (verified against commit a930b8a, the HEAD at the start of this research session): `emphasis.iconStyle.borderColor: tokens.color.accent50` is at line 144, and the normal `iconStyle.borderColor: tokens.color.accent50` is at line 139. IMPORTANT: the repository has moved forward while I was researching — the current checkout (HEAD e3a635d) already contains commit 3acecdd "impl: toolbox-emphasis-color", which applied exactly this accent50→accent70 change to line 144, and also added /workspace/requirement_patches/toolbox-emphasis-color.diff. If the engineer works from the current tree the edit is already a no-op; confirm the starting state with `grep -n "accent" src/component/toolbox/ToolboxModel.ts` before editing. Two `accent50` occurrences nine lines apart make a naive find-and-replace dangerous — only the one nested under `emphasis` may change; changing line 139 as well would reintroduce the collapse at a different color. Overlap with other requirements: several dark-mode requirements are in flight in this same repo (commits 9049644 darkmode-lightness-algorithm, a5603ab visualmap-darkmode-inrange, e3a635d matrix-darkmode-colors) and they touch /workspace/src/visual/tokens.ts and /workspace/src/theme/dark.ts — in particular the accent dark-mode transform at tokens.ts:209-217 was recently rewritten, so the optional dark.ts step may conflict; keep it in a separate commit or skip it. Ambiguity: the requirement names no specific color, only "a clearly different visual highlight"; accent70 is inferred from the timeline component's existing accent50/accent70 normal-vs-emphasis convention, so a reviewer expecting a different shade (e.g. accent60 or accent75) would still be satisfied by the acceptance signal.
